name: Complex_Cube_Roots
questiontext:
Consider the complex number \[z = {{CT:0}}.\] Give the modulus and argument of all its cube roots.
Use each row in the table below to specify a cube root, with the modulus in the first column and the argument in the second. Each argument should be entered as a multiple of \(\pi\) and should fall in the interval \([-\pi,\pi ]\). [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: each entry in its own box: a number, a fraction (e.g. 1/2) or an expression (e.g. sqrt(2)).
generalfeedback:
For the complex number \[z = {{CT:0}}\] The modulus \(|z| = {{CT:1}}\) and the argument of \(z = {{CT:2}}\)
Therefore the cube roots of \(z\) have a modulus of \[\sqrt[3]{z} = \sqrt[3]{{CT:1}} = {{CT:3}}\] \[\] The arguments of \(z = {{CT:2}}\) or \({{CT:4}}\) or \({{CT:5}}\)
Giving the arguments of the cube roots as \( \frac{{CT:2}}{3}\) ,\(\frac{{CT:4}}{3}\) and \(\frac{{CT:5}}{3}\) equal to \({{CT:6}}\),\({{CT:7}}\),\({{CT:8}}\).
